notes: Increased sensor size to 0.016 m and shifted sensor positions forward by +0.01 m to improve early line detection and reduce line loss events, especially on the slalom track. PID gains slightly reduced kp to 8 to moderate steering oscillation. Observation requests expanded to include control effort for better control smoothness assessment.
rationale: The previous iteration's race data showed that the robot performed well on the oval and s-bend tracks but struggled significantly on the slalom track, with frequent line loss events (1.05 average) and no finishes. Steering oscillation was moderate to high, especially on the s-bend and slalom tracks, indicating some instability in control. To address these issues, I increased the sensor size from 0.012 m to 0.016 m to improve line coverage and reduce line loss events. Additionally, I shifted all sensor positions forward by +0.01 m in the y-direction to enable earlier line detection, which should help improve progress and reduce steering oscillation. The number of sensors and their lateral spacing remain unchanged to maintain resolution and coverage. The wheel track, wheel radius, body dimensions, and mass are kept the same to preserve stability and handling characteristics. The controller uses a PID scheme with gains tuned to balance responsiveness and smoothness, and sensor weights are set symmetrically to emphasize outer sensors for edge detection. The line loss recovery strategy is set to 'search_left' to steer right when the line is lost, consistent with prior effective behavior. Observation requests include completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, steering_oscillation, and control_effort to comprehensively evaluate performance and control smoothness.
